CRLR No.727 of 2022
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, 
Advocate for the revisionist. 
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, 
Advocate for the respondent. 
The revisionist proposes to 
challenge the order dated 06.08.2022, 
passed in Misc. Criminal Case No.59 
of 2018, Smt. Pragya Chaubey and 
another vs. Om Shiva Chaubey, by the 
court of Judge, Family Court, 
Khatima, District Udham Singh 
Nagar. By it, an application for interim 
maintenance filed by the revisionist 
no.1 has been allowed and the 
respondent has been directed to pay 
`21,100/- per month to the 
revisionists (`15,000/- per month to 
the revisionist no.1 and `6,000/- per 
month to the revisionist no.2).
The revision is delayed. A Delay 
Condonation Application No.1 of 2022 
has been filed. 
It is the case of the revisionists 
that the revisionist no.1 has to arrange 
the finance to prefer the revision and 
in that process delay occurred. 
Having considered the grounds, 
this Court is of the view that the delay 
in filing revision may be condoned. 
Accordingly, the Delay 
Condonation Application (IA) No.1 of 
2022 is allowed.
Delay in filing the criminal 
revision is condoned.  Admit the revision.
The respondent is being 
represented. 
Call for the LCR. 
List this case on 29.04.2023. 
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 03.01.2023
Sanjay

Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, learned 
counsel for the revisionist in CRLR No. 
727 of 2022.
2. Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned 
counsel for the revisionist in CRLR No. 
572 of 2022. 
3. Both the parties were married on
20.1.2016 and due to some differences 
in between them both are living 
separately since 2018 i.e. almost more 
than eight years. There is one issue 
from their marriage, the son who is 
living with the wife. As on date the total 
amount towards the arrears of 
maintenance is about Rs. 9,19,000/-.
The husband is getting monthly salary 
in hand about Rs. 1,10,000/-. 
4. In such an eventuality, the 
husband is directed to clear the entire 
arrears of maintenance and in this 
regard he shall pay Rs. 30,000/-
towards the arrears of maintenance
every month and in addition to this he 
shall also pay regular maintenance of 
Rs. 21,000/- in total i.e. Rs. 51,000/-
(30,000+21,000) in the first week of  every month. 
5. In the meantime, since both the 
parties are mature and are having a 
son, therefore, this Court is of the view 
that they are the best person to resolve 
their matrimonial dispute in order to 
secure the future of son. Let both the 
parties may think over it sincerely, in 
order to settle their differences.
6. List this case on 20.04.2026.
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
17.03.2026
Nahid
